title: Inheritance and Alibi Anew
premise: Mara Vasquez, the coroner of the fading town of Hollow Creek, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a murder he insists will be pinned on him. The victim, according to every record Mara can find, died eleven years ago: Elise Brandt, the heiress whose inheritance built half the town. As Mara digs into sealed autopsy files and a witness list everyone swears is empty, they discover Elise may have faked her death to escape her family's empire — and that someone in Hollow Creek has been quietly killing everyone who ever saw her alive. When the stranger turns up dead in Mara's own morgue drawer, framed for murders committed in his name, Mara must find the living witness before the killer completes the erasure. In the end, Mara exposes the town's beloved patriarch as the architect of both deaths, but chooses to let Elise remain 'dead,' protecting her new identity at the cost of the truth's full light.
about_author: Vesper Iversen is the pen name of a former rural paramedic who spent a decade answering calls in towns too small to have their own police force. They write mysteries about people whose quiet competence hides how much death they've witnessed.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A pale, sweating man named Daniel Okafor arrives at the morgue after hours, offering an absurd retainer: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. He won't name the victim, only slides over a photograph of a woman and says, 'Her name was already on your books once.' Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional skepticism.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishing Hollow Creek's rhythms — the cemetery Mara tends like a garden, the town's dependence on the Brandt family fortune. Mara searches records and finds Elise Brandt's death certificate, dated eleven years ago, signed by Mara's predecessor. Beat: the past pressing its weight on the present.

chapters.title: A Death Already Served
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The old file on Elise Brandt is thin, too clean: closed casket, out-of-town medical examiner, no family request for review. Mara notices the signature of the attending witness — a name that matches Daniel Okafor's employer listing. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mara and Deputy Corinne Ash, Mara's reluctant ally. Interviews at the diner and feed store reveal Elise as either saint or ghost — no one will say her name without glancing at the Brandt estate on the hill. Beat: a town complicit in its own silence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There Yet
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Flashback chapters begin: three weeks earlier, Daniel received letters written in his own handwriting that he never wrote, describing murders scheduled like appointments. He came to Mara because she was the only official in the county with no ties to the Brandt trust. Beat: dread of being pre-framed.

chapters.title: Exhumation Weather
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara petitions for exhumation; Judge Pell, whose campaign the Brandts funded, stalls for ten days then grants it with conditions. The grave holds a coffin weighted with sandbags and a stranger's bones. Beat: vindication curdling into fear — someone powerful approved this lie.

chapters.title: Bones That Don't Belong
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, forensic detail. The skeleton is female, mid-thirties, but the dental work doesn't match Elise's charts. Someone dug up a Jane Doe from two counties away. Mara realizes the frame-up around Daniel requires a body — and one is being prepared. Beat: the murder clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Letters in My Hand
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel finds a fourth letter predicting a death at the reservoir, dated tomorrow. He goes anyway and finds not a body but a witness: a woman in a headscarf watching from the treeline, who flees when he calls out. Beat: hope — the dead may be walking.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cross-referencing the original case, Mara identifies Rosa Ilić, the night nurse listed as witnessing Elise's death — a woman who left town abruptly and whose forwarding address dissolves into nothing. Corinne admits the sheriff's office was ordered to stop looking for her years ago. Beat: institutional rot revealed.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Patriarch
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. August Brandt, Elise's grandfather and the town's benefactor, invites Mara to the estate — charm layered over threat. He mentions Mara's late mother's debts, offers to clear them, asks casually about the exhumation. Beat: power extending its hand and showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Rosa in the Glass
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Interlude: Rosa, living under a new name two towns over, has spent eleven years paid to stay silent about what she saw the night Elise 'died' — that the body on the table was breathing. A letter arrives in handwriting she recognizes as Elise's. Beat: guilt waking from long sleep.

chapters.title: Two Funerals Deep
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The reservoir yields its real body: the county's retired archivist, the man who filed Elise's false death certificate, drowned and staged to implicate Daniel. Mara's forensic findings contradict the sheriff's tidy narrative publicly. Beat: Mara crosses from observer to target.

chapters.title: Ash and Alibi
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. Corinne runs Daniel's alibi for the archivist's murder and finds it airtight — which terrifies her, because whoever built the frame knew the alibi would hold. She discovers the sheriff's department has been receiving anonymous 'tips' for weeks, all in the same neat hand. Beat: the conspiracy has administrative reach.

chapters.title: The Night Nurse's Confession
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa comes to Mara at night, terrified, and tells the truth: Elise woke on the embalming table, drugged but alive, and bribed Rosa with the only currency that mattered — evidence against August Brandt's laundering operation. Elise vanished; Rosa took hush money and shame. Beat: the mystery's spine exposed.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel confesses why he's entangled: he was Elise's lover before her disappearance, hired by her years later through cutouts to prepare her legal resurrection — proof of identity, not innocence. The letters framing him are someone intercepting her plan. Beat: love as both motive and vulnerability.

chapters.title: What August Built
chapters.summary: Mara and Corinne's alternating POV. Following the money, they map the Brandt trust's laundering network — and realize every person killed or silenced since Elise's disappearance touched the ledger. August isn't hiding a murder; he's completing an eleven-year cleanup. Beat: scale of corruption fully visible.

chapters.title: The Trap Wears My Face
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel is arrested for the archivist's murder on fabricated forensics; in holding, he's offered freedom in exchange for recanting everything and naming Elise as alive and fraudulent. He refuses. Beat: duty and love collide — his silence protects her, his words destroy them both.

chapters.title: Graveyard Meeting
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the cemetery at midnight, the woman from the treeline appears: Elise Brandt, alive, weathered, furious that her plan endangered others. She carries the ledger originals. Mara must decide whether the law she serves or the justice the town needs comes first. Beat: the moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Corinne and Mara's POV. August learns Rosa talked; his men move to erase her and burn the archive. Mara and Corinne have less than a day to secure the ledger, spring Daniel, and get Rosa somewhere safe — while the sheriff, bought long ago, looks the other way. Beat: breathless escalation toward climax.

chapters.title: The Weight of the Coffin
chapters.summary: Climax, Mara's POV. Confrontation at the Brandt mausoleum, where August intends to stage Elise's 'return' and death on his terms — a second funeral to bury the first lie forever. Mara trades the ledger's location for Rosa's life, then reveals the county recorder has had certified copies since dawn. Beat: the corrupt patriarch undone by paperwork and nerve.

chapters.title: Verdicts and Vacancies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, aftermath. August is indicted; the sheriff resigns; Daniel walks free but chooses to leave town rather than testify to loving a dead woman. Elise, legally still deceased, asks Mara what should be carved on her real grave someday. Beat: bittersweet cost accounting of the truth.

chapters.title: A New Name on Old Ground
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, coda. Months later, Mara buries the Jane Doe whose bones lent Elise her death, giving her a name and a stone at last. A postcard arrives, unsigned, from a coastal town: 'Some inheritances are chosen.' Mara locks the morgue and walks home under a sky finally ordinary. Beat: quiet resolution — identity as something you give yourself.
